name: Cable crunch
cue: Curl your ribs down toward your pelvis and keep your hips still.
research: research.json biomech.cable_crunch: kneeling on a mat facing a high pulley (2.0 m), knees ~0.44 H (78 cm) from the column (research 45-60 cm; farther so the head clears the column by at least 0.05 H through the rep, skinChecks), thighs 20 deg forward of vertical and frozen, shins on the mat, tops of the feet down. Rope held beside the ears, elbows forward and down, hands glued to the head through the rep. The rep is a segmental spinal curl, never a hip hinge: the upper thoracic spine flexes first (via key M), then the lumbar spine, then the pelvis tucks back (hip flexion 84 -> 64, so the hip angle opens while the trunk curls); the return reverses the order (via key N). Thorax tilt 56 -> 112 deg, spinal flexion -8 -> 68 (research -10 -> 60), hip-to-C7 chord 53 -> 79 deg (research 55 -> 80), grips 0.95 -> 0.57 m above the floor (research 0.85-0.95 -> 0.45-0.5; spinal flexion is taken to 68, the top of its research band, and the pelvis tucks to hip 64; deeper would leave the band). Because the hands ride on the head, they move down and slightly forward rather than back toward the knees, so the cable stays within 2 deg of vertical (research 20-30 deg at the bottom) and the elbows end about 0.15 H in front of the knees. The weight stack rides on the column as its guide rod. The rope knot rides on the cable line above the head (it slides in the thorax frame as the cable angle changes); the stack rises by the cable shortening. Geometry: tools/design/cable_crunch.mjs.

targets.note: Research trunk_flexion is the hip-to-C7 chord (55 -> 80), checked as trunk_chord; research trunk_spinal_flexion (-10 -> 60) is checked as spinal_flexion (thorax tilt minus pelvis tilt). The engine trunk_flexion is the thorax tilt (56 -> 112 here) and is not a target. Shoulder abduction is not checked: above 90 deg of elevation the read-back abduction angle wraps past 90 (research flexion 125 + abduction 20 is an arm plane of 81 deg; 72 here).

camera.note: Research view is the right profile of the lifter (az 90, el 5), which shows the spinal curl with frozen hips. The abs face the floor, so the view turns 18 deg toward the front and drops 17 deg below belly height (az 72, el -12, 24.7 deg in all): the rectus reads along the underside of the curling trunk from the ribs to the pelvis, between the near thigh and the near arm. The reduced-motion still is motion.still, half-way through the concentric (spinal flexion 46 of 68 deg, hip-to-C7 chord 76): at the peak the curled trunk turns the belly to the floor, edge-on to every view inside the 30 deg budget (a sweep over az 62-90, el -4 to -24 gained at most 2 % there), while half-way the rectus reads as a band from the groin to the ribs. Phone stage glow ~980 CSS px at the stretch, ~665 at the still, ~615 at the peak. The camera sits below the floor plane, so floor-level parts show their undersides across the horizon arc: at el -17 (1165 / 775 / 685 px) the kneeling pad and column foot hid 49 % of the arc (the old full floor plate 86 %), at el -12 36 %, at el -8 9 % (but 26 % less glow at the still). A more frontal azimuth (az 45-60) showed less rectus at the peak (the curled trunk turns the belly away and the elbows cover the upper rectus) and lit the curled back so that bare skin outshone the glow. fill 0.55 and shiftX -0.06 move the figure left so the column and the weight stack stay inside the right edge; the high pulley stays above the frame (fitting it would shrink the figure to about half). The obliques (research secondary) are not drawn: in this view they cover the flank next to the rectus and outshine it.

skinChecks.note: knees and shins stay on the mat
tops of the toes rest on the mat
head stays clear of the column at every phase
